SMTO-CFG-0033 — SMTO's settings file is from a newer version of SMTO

GUID: 4b1e364b-53ce-4a4e-a6f0-3f07881677d5
Slug: config-config-version-is-newer-than-this-runtime
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The startup settings file (usually config.yaml) was written for a newer SMTO than the one installed, so SMTO stopped instead of guessing what it means. The file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages SMTO which version created this settings file, then update SMTO to that version or newer by running its installer. A newer SMTO understands the newer file format, so it can start with these settings.
  2. If you must stay on this version, put back a settings file made for it, such as the copy you used before, then start SMTO again. This version only reads settings files in the format it was built for.
  3. If it still stops, select Copy error details on the startup screen, or copy the full message from the window where SMTO was started. The message shows the file's format number and the numbers this SMTO supports.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied message to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change the config_version number to force SMTO to start; the file may hold settings this version would misread.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration validation failed because config_version in the application YAML is greater than APP_CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION supported by this build.

What this means

  • Application config_version exceeds APP_CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION after normalization. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Application config_version exceeds APP_CONFIG_CURRENT_VERSION after normalization.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved version with the installed build's supported range before changing either.

How to fix it

  • Read config_version in the file selected by --config, AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH or the working-directory config.yaml and compare it with the supported range in the message. Run a build that supports that version, or restore a configuration written for this build; do not relabel the version without migrating the content. Validate offline with aor doctor --config and the file's path.
  • Use a build supporting this configuration or a deliberately migrated compatible configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A compatible configuration/build pair validates without simply relabeling an unmigrated file.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
